neighbours.label: movement/behaviour verbs in field-guide descriptions of birds and small animals (pausing, flight, mobbing)
fire: The plover runs a few steps across the mudflat and then pauses to pick at the surface.
Low and buoyant in flight, the tern beats its wings steadily over the waves.
When an owl is discovered by day, crows gather around it in noisy mobbing flocks.
The thrush hops through the leaf litter, stopping now and then to listen for worms.
Heron: stalks slowly through the shallows before striking at fish with its bill.
Shrews forage by darting under logs and pausing briefly to sniff the soil.
If disturbed at the nest, the grebe slips quietly into the water and dives.
Swifts are almost always seen flying high, wheeling in tight circles after insects.
quiet: The plover has a short black bill, sandy upperparts and a white collar around the neck.
The tern is pale grey above with a black cap and a deeply forked white tail.
Crows are large black birds with stout bills and glossy, slightly purple feathers.
The thrush has a brown back, a cream breast and bold dark spots along its flanks.
Heron: tall grey bird with long yellow legs, a dagger bill and a black head stripe.
Shrews are tiny mammals with velvety grey fur, a long snout and very small eyes.
The grebe has a rufous neck in summer and a short, sharply pointed dark bill.
Swifts have long scythe-shaped wings, short forked tails and dark sooty plumage.
